name: MK-0773

lead: MK-0773 is an investigational SARM that was tested for sarcopenia, the loss of muscle with age. It was designed to act on muscle with less effect on other tissues.
In the one published efficacy trial, 170 older women gained lean mass compared with placebo, but strength and physical function did not improve beyond placebo.

paras: It is a steroidal androgen receptor ligand picked from a large screen of compounds for partial, tissue-selective activity.
Safety data from the efficacy trial are not detailed in the sources reviewed. It is not approved for any use and is covered by anti-doping testing.

lead: MK-0773, also known as PF-05314882, is an experimental steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) that was developed to increase muscle mass and strength while minimizing effects on other tissues. It was tested in clinical trials for sarcopenia, the age-related loss of muscle mass and function.[1][2]

Its discovery was reported in 2010 as the product of a screening strategy using more than 1,000 synthetic androgen receptor ligands to look for compounds whose anabolic and reproductive-tissue effects were separable.[3] In a phase 2A trial in 170 frail older women with sarcopenia, it increased lean body mass compared with placebo, but this did not translate into improved strength or physical function.[1] The compound is not approved for any use.

paras: MK-0773 is an androgen receptor ligand chosen using the idea that anabolic effects in muscle and effects in reproductive tissue depend on different transcriptional requirements, so a partial agonist might separate them.[3]

The one published efficacy trial found lean mass gains without functional benefit (see Clinical studies).[1] A 2025 systematic review of randomized trials of SARMs on physical performance covers this class of compounds more broadly.[4]

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2A trial (NCT00529659, started 2007) enrolled 170 women aged 65 or older with sarcopenia and moderate physical dysfunction. Participants received MK-0773 at 50 mg twice daily or placebo for six months, and all received vitamin D and protein supplementation.[1][5] MK-0773 produced a statistically significant increase in lean body mass versus placebo, but the authors concluded this did not translate into better strength or function, and noted that improvements in the placebo group may be partly attributable to the supplements.[1]

Two phase 1 trials are also registered as completed: one in healthy postmenopausal women (67 participants, listed under osteoporosis, begun 2005) and one in healthy older men (68 participants, begun 2007). Their results are not summarized in the sources reviewed.[6][7] A review of SARMs for cancer-related muscle wasting also discusses the compound class.[8]

Doping-control researchers have identified in vitro phase I metabolites of MK-0773 to support detection, and SARMs are covered by anti-doping surveillance.[9][10] The sources reviewed do not document use of MK-0773 in looksmaxxing communities.

timeline.event: Phase 1 study in healthy postmenopausal women begins.[6]
Phase 2 sarcopenia trial and a phase 1 study in older men begin.[5][7]
